note: GTA 6 released 19 November 2026. Guides below are written from the official trophy descriptions and the game's trailers; where a precise location, count, or step is still being confirmed by the community, the guide says so rather than inventing a detail.

trophies.guide: Earn the other 54 trophies on the list and this platinum unlocks automatically. There is no shortcut: it requires the story, all 100% completion work, the collectibles, and the activity trophies. Plan the platinum in three passes — story first, then the missable-adjacent and partner trophies, then the long grinds like 250 stunts and the card sets — and use the tracker's roadmap to keep the order straight. Nothing on the list is permanently missable as far as the community has confirmed, so you can clean up in free roam after the story.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!

trophies.guide: Play through the opening mission 'Gone Fishing', which introduces Lucia and Jason and the state of Leonida. The trophy pops when the mission's final cutscene ends, so just follow the on-screen objectives — there is no optional objective to worry about. It is the first story trophy and cannot be missed.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise

trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 1. The chapter trophy unlocks automatically when the last Chapter 1 mission completes and the chapter title card for the next chapter appears. If you get stuck on a mission, you can lower the difficulty or skip a failed mission after several attempts from the pause menu, as in previous GTA games. Chapter progress is tracked in the pause menu under Stats.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost

trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 2. This is a story-progression trophy that unlocks when the final Chapter 2 mission ends; no side content is required for it. Keep playing the gold story markers (L for Lucia, J for Jason) and it will pop on its own. As with all chapter trophies, it cannot be missed.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money

trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 3. The trophy unlocks at the end of the chapter's final mission. Chapter 3 is where the story moves firmly into Vice City itself, so expect more missions in the city and on the beachfront. No collectibles or side activities are needed for this trophy.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!

trophies.guide: Finish every story mission in Chapter 4. This is the last chapter trophy before the finale, and it pops when the final Chapter 4 mission wraps up. After it unlocks, the remaining story mission leads into the gold 'You Gotta Know When to Get Off' trophy for the final mission. Keep following the story markers and do not worry about side content yet.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma

trophies.guide: Complete the final story mission of GTA 6. The mission unlocks after Chapter 4, and the trophy pops when its closing cutscene finishes. This is a gold trophy because it marks the end of the main story, not because the mission itself is especially hard — if you fail, you can retry from the last checkpoint. After the credits, free roam continues, so any unfinished side content can still be completed.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission 'Breakfast Run'. The trophy unlocks when the mission ends, so follow the objectives and the waypoint as usual. If you fail the mission, retrying from the checkpoint still counts — the trophy only cares that the mission is completed, not how many attempts it took. Mission replays are available after finishing the story if you ever need to revisit it.
trophies.name: Trust

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission 'The Cartel Heist'. Heist missions in GTA 6 are multi-stage, so expect a setup phase followed by the heist itself; the trophy pops at the end of the whole mission, not after the setup. Bring your best weapons and keep an eye on your partner's position during the escape, since heist finales usually end with a chase. Failing and retrying still counts.
trophies.name: Break the Bank

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission 'Child's Play'. Follow the mission waypoint and objectives through to the final cutscene. This is a straightforward story trophy: it unlocks the first time you finish the mission, regardless of your medal or how many times you retried. If you are playing for 100% completion later, note that mission medals are tracked separately from this trophy.
trophies.name: Family Matters

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission 'Headliners'. The trophy unlocks when the mission's final sequence ends. As with other named story missions, there is no special requirement beyond finishing it — the trophy is not tied to a medal, a time limit, or an optional objective. If you fail, retry from the checkpoint and the trophy will still unlock on completion.
trophies.name: DWNFALL

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission 'VCIA Takedown', set around Vice City International Airport. Expect a combat-heavy mission with airport security and law enforcement responding quickly, so stock up on armor and ammunition beforehand. The trophy pops when the mission ends. Note that this is a different activity from the free-roam 'Catch Me If You Can' trophy, which is about making an unscheduled departure from VCIA on your own.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission 'Operation Savage Glory'. The name suggests a large-scale set piece, so expect heavy combat and possibly vehicle sections; take your time, use cover, and let checkpoints do their work if you fail. The trophy unlocks at the end of the mission and cannot be missed, since story missions can be replayed after the credits.
trophies.name: Snow Storm

trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion as shown in the pause menu under Stats. In GTA games this means finishing the story, all stranger missions, the collectibles, the activities, and the miscellaneous checklist items the game counts — the exact checklist is still being mapped by the community now that the game has only just released on 19 November 2026, so use an up-to-date community checklist alongside this tracker. This is the longest grind on the list and the second gold trophy; save it for last, after the story and all other trophies, and check your Stats percentage regularly to see what is left.
trophies.name: A Long Road

trophies.guide: Perform 250 stunts across Leonida. Stunts are the game's trick system — jumps, near misses, wheelies, drifts, and airtime all count, and the game tracks a running total. The fastest way is to find a good jump spot and repeat it: a fast car or bike, a ramp or hill, and a clean landing racks up stunts quickly, and the count carries across sessions. This is a grind, so chip away at it while travelling between missions rather than leaving all 250 for the end.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try every type of side activity at least once. The community is still confirming the exact list of activity types the game counts, but it includes the activities named elsewhere on this list — racing, fishing, shooting range, drone racing, arcade games, bowling, meditation, and hunting. Visit one of each and the trophy pops; you do not need to win or complete them, just try them. Work through the tracker checklist one activity at a time and tick each off as you sample it.
trophies.name: Master of None

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in every Shooting Range challenge. The exact number of challenges is still being confirmed by the community, but the starter data lists 42, so expect dozens of timed target courses across the ranges in Leonida. Gold medals require accuracy and speed: take your time on the first shots, learn each course's target layout, and replay a course until the gold threshold is met — progress is per-challenge, so you can gold them one at a time. Use a weapon you are comfortable with and keep your aim steady rather than rushing.
trophies.name: The Shootist

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at every race location. The starter data lists 14 locations across Leonida; each one is a separate race you must win, not just enter. Drone races are about smooth lines through the rings — cut corners where the course allows, keep the drone low through gates, and learn each course's layout before going for the win. If you lose a race, you can retry it immediately, so work through the locations one by one.
trophies.name: Top Fun

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — 20 distinct race events, not the same race 20 times. Races are found at race markers around Leonida and include street races and other vehicle events; each unique race you win counts once. Vary your vehicle for the course: a fast car for highway circuits, something nimble for tight city routes. Track which races you have already won so you do not waste time repeating one.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Fishing is one of Leonida's side activities: find a fishing spot, start the challenge against Cal, and out-fish him by landing more or bigger fish within the challenge's rules. The exact mechanics are still being documented by the community since the game only just released, so expect a timing and reeling mini-game similar to fishing in other open-world games. If you lose, challenge him again — the trophy only needs one win.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle

trophies.guide: Complete a single arcade game at an arcade in Leonida. Arcades are found in Vice City and other towns; walk up to a cabinet, start a game, and play it through to its end — 'complete' means finishing the game, not just starting it. Any arcade game counts, so pick the one you find easiest. This is one of the quickest trophies on the list and also counts toward trying every activity type.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete Andy's mission strand through to its final mission. Andy is one of the stranger/associate characters who gives a chain of missions; his missions appear as a marker on the map, and each one unlocks the next. Work through the chain in order and the trophy pops when the last mission ends. These strands are available in free roam after they first appear, so you can finish Andy's chain whenever you like.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete Kenton's mission strand through to its final mission. Kenton's chain involves boats — the trophy name is a nod to a famous movie line about a boat accident — so expect water-based missions and possibly a chase on the water. Follow his map markers through the chain in order; the trophy unlocks when the final mission's closing scene ends. Like the other character strands, it can be finished in free roam.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete Billy's mission strand through to its final mission. Billy's chain is the biker strand of the game, so expect motorcycle missions and rides with his crew. Play through his missions in order as they appear on the map, and the trophy pops at the end of the final one. A fast, well-handling bike helps on the riding sections, but the trophy only requires completing the missions.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 stranger mission strands across Leonida. Strangers appear as '?' markers on the map; each one is a small chain of missions with its own oddball character, in the tradition of GTA's Strangers and Freaks. You need 8 complete strands, not just 8 missions — finish a stranger's whole chain before moving on, and keep a note of which ones you have completed. The character strands for Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, and Tyrone are separate trophies, so those five plus three more stranger chains will get you there.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete Randy's mission strand through to its final mission. Randy's chain is about supply runs, so expect deliveries and pickups across Leonida with rival crews getting in the way. Follow his markers in order and the trophy pops when the last mission ends. It can be completed in free roam at any point after the strand first appears.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete Tyrone's mission strand through to its final mission. Tyrone's chain is tied to the music and club scene — the name is a DJ reference — so expect missions around Vice City's nightlife. Play through his missions in order as they appear, and the trophy unlocks at the end of the final one. Like the other character strands, it remains available in free roam.
trophies.name: Spin On This!

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every meditation spot across Leonida. The starter data lists 18 spots; each is a scenic location — beaches, hilltops, and quiet corners of the state — where you can sit and meditate. The trophy pops when you have meditated at all of them, so you will need a map or community list of the spots, since they are not all marked by default. This is a relaxing collectible-style trophy: work through the spots region by region while you are exploring for other trophies.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. Bret is the hunting contact: he will ask you to track down a specific rare animal somewhere in Leonida's wilderness. Expect a tracking sequence — follow signs, stay downwind, and take a clean shot when you find it. The exact animal and location are still being confirmed by the community, so check an up-to-date guide before you go; a scoped rifle and patience are the tools for the job. The trophy pops when the hunt is delivered to Bret.
trophies.name: Fair Game

trophies.guide: Complete 3 full collectible card sets. Cards are scattered across Leonida — in shops, on tables, and tucked into hidden spots — and each set needs every card in it. This is a silver trophy because it takes real searching: use a community card map, collect set by set, and check your collection progress in the menu to see which cards you are still missing. You need three complete sets, not just three cards, so focus on finishing one set at a time.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck

trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK It feature at 100 different locations across Leonida. WAiNK It is the game's photo or tagging-style activity at scenic and notable spots — find the prompt at a location, activate it, and move on to the next. The count is cumulative and tracked across sessions, so you can chip away at it while exploring for other trophies. A community map of the 100 locations will help, since the exact spots are still being documented now that the game has just released.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!

trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges. Challenges are the game's small objectives — driving feats, combat feats, exploration goals, and activity milestones — tracked in the challenges menu. They accumulate naturally as you play, and 50 is reachable well before the end of a full playthrough if you vary what you do. Check the challenges list regularly and pick off easy ones (like driving a certain distance or visiting places) to push the count up.
trophies.name: One Last Thing

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner (Lucia or Jason) beside you, build up a 4-star wanted level and then lose it. Get the cops to 4 stars — robbing, shooting, or causing chaos in a busy area will do it — then escape with your partner still with you: break line of sight, get out of the search area, and stay hidden until the stars clear. Doing it with your partner is the key requirement, so make sure they are actually following you before you start the escape. A fast car and a quiet hiding spot, like the countryside or a tunnel, make the escape much easier.
trophies.name: Hot Together

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: With your partner, rob 3 shops back-to-back without your wanted level ever clearing in between — the wording is ambiguous and the community is still confirming whether the requirement is to keep the wanted level or to never gain one, so read the trophy's exact phrasing in-game and check an up-to-date guide before attempting it. The most likely reading is that you must keep a wanted level through all three robberies: pick three shops close together in Vice City, rob the first, then drive straight to the next while the cops are still after you, and repeat for the third. Do not let the stars clear between robberies, and keep your partner with you. A fast getaway car parked outside each shop helps enormously.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy

trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles. 'Discover' means encountering a new vehicle type — driving it, or at least getting close enough for the game to register it. Leonida has a huge vehicle roster, from beat-up sedans to supercars, boats, and planes, so the count climbs fast if you drive everything you see. Visit car parks, dealerships, the airport, and the docks to find rarer types, and check your vehicle collection progress in the menu to see what you are missing.
trophies.name: Whip It Good

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies during a single use of Combat Focus. Combat Focus is GTA 6's slow-motion aiming mode: activate it when you are facing a group of enemies, then drop five of them before the effect ends. The easiest setup is a gang shootout or a wanted-level standoff where enemies bunch together — wait until several are in view, trigger Combat Focus, and work through them quickly with headshots. If you only get four, release and try again; the trophy needs all five in one activation.
trophies.name: Gunslinger

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure from Vice City International Airport — that is, take off in a plane without going through the normal channels. Get a plane at VCIA, get it onto a runway, and take off; the game registers the 'unscheduled departure' when you leave the airport airspace in the aircraft. Expect a wanted level the moment you do it, so have an escape plan for after takeoff. Any flyable plane at the airport should work.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can

trophies.guide: The community is still confirming the exact requirement for this one — the description is a joke, not a checklist — so check an up-to-date guide before attempting it. The leading theory is that it involves the Rhino tank: either destroying one, surviving one, or taking one for a drive. A practical approach is to build up a high wanted level until a Rhino is deployed, then either destroy it with sticky bombs or steal it and drive it around; either way, expect heavy resistance and keep your distance from its cannon. If the trophy does not pop from that, the confirmed method will be in the community guides within days of launch.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. This is a stealth robbery: enter the store quietly, avoid the cameras and the staff's line of sight, take the jewelry, and leave without anyone raising the alarm. Go at a quiet time, move slowly, and do not draw a weapon or smash a case in front of a witness. If you are spotted, leave and try again — the trophy only counts a clean, undetected robbery.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape after each one. Bank vault robberies are the bigger heist-style robberies in free roam: find a bank, get into the vault, grab the cash, and escape the police response. Each completed vault robbery counts once, and you need five in total — they do not need to be in a row or in one session. Plan each one: a fast car outside, a route out of the area, and enough armor and ammo for the escape. This is a silver trophy because five full vault jobs take real preparation.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape. Armored trucks drive set routes around Leonida — spot one on the road, block it or force it to stop, then break into the back and grab the cash before the police arrive. Sticky bombs on the rear doors are the classic method, but any way of opening the truck works. Once you have the money, lose the wanted level to complete the escape, and the trophy pops. If the truck gets away, just find another one.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play

trophies.guide: Explore every area of Leonida. The starter data lists 52 areas, covering Vice City, the beaches, the swamps, the Keys, and the countryside towns. An area counts once you have visited it, and the game tracks your exploration in the map or stats menu. The practical way to do it is to drive or fly a route that touches every named region — a helicopter or plane makes the remote areas much quicker — and check the map for grey, unvisited patches. This pairs naturally with the meditation spots and the vehicle discovery trophy.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each gang. The starter data lists 9 gangs in Leonida, and each one runs illegal operations — stash houses, drug labs, or smuggling spots — that you can raid. You need one robbery per gang, not one per operation, so find a single operation for each of the 9 gangs and rob it. The exact gang list and operation locations are still being mapped by the community, so use an up-to-date guide to identify which gang owns each spot before you hit it.
trophies.name: Pest Control

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach. Head to a bar or beachfront spot on Ocean Beach in Vice City, order a cocktail, and drink it while looking out over the water. The trophy's name is a nod to the beginning of the game — the first trailer's famous beach shot — so it is a small, scenic moment rather than a challenge. Any beachfront bar on Ocean Beach should work; sit, order, and the trophy pops once the drink is enjoyed with the view.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. Drive a car into a vehicle showroom, then smash straight back out through the glass front — the 'classic style' is the old GTA trick of driving through a dealership window. Pick a showroom with a big glass frontage, build up speed inside or just outside, and drive through it. The trophy pops when you break out through the showroom front in a vehicle. You may get a wanted level, so have an escape in mind.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Play bowling at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley. Find the alley, start a game of bowling, and complete it — 'follow-through' is the trophy's hint that you need to actually finish a game, not just throw one ball. Bowling is one of the returning activities from GTA IV, so expect a simple aim-and-power mini-game. This also counts toward trying every activity type for the 'Master of None' trophy.
trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling

trophies.guide: Build a partnership with mass appeal — the trophy is about Lucia and Jason's partnership reaching a milestone of public attention. The community is still confirming the exact trigger, but it is tied to the duo's social-media-style presence in the game (the in-game social network, where their exploits gain followers). Keep playing the story and the partner activities, and check an up-to-date guide for the exact requirement; it is likely to unlock naturally during a full playthrough.
trophies.name: Personal Best

trophies.guide: Make choices — the description, 'Choices made (for better or worse)', tracks a count of choices you make in missions and free roam, such as sparing or confronting someone, or picking one approach over another. The community is still confirming the exact number the trophy requires (the starter data notes a count toward 500), so keep choosing whenever the game offers a decision and the trophy will unlock as the count climbs. This is a long-term tracker that fills up naturally over a full playthrough, not something to grind in one sitting — but if you want to speed it up, favour the missions and stranger encounters that present explicit choices.
trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder

trophies.guide: Succeed on the second try. This trophy is about failing something once and then succeeding on the immediate retry — the classic 'second time's the charm'. The community is still confirming exactly which activity it tracks, but the natural way to get it is to fail a mission or challenge once and then complete it on the next attempt. It is very likely to unlock on its own during normal play, since everyone fails a mission at least once; if it has not popped by the end of the story, retry any mission you previously failed and complete it.
trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess

trophies.guide: Witness something strange. Leonida is full of easter eggs and weird encounters — UFO sightings, cryptids in the swamps, and other X-Files-style moments — and this trophy pops when you stumble into one of them. The community is still mapping exactly which encounter triggers it, so check an up-to-date easter egg guide for a confirmed location; the swamps and the remote countryside are the usual places for this kind of thing. It is a one-off moment trophy, so once you know the spot, just go there and let the event play out.
trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone over with a melee drive-by — that is, hit a pedestrian with a melee weapon while driving past in a vehicle. Get a melee weapon equipped, drive slowly past a pedestrian on a sidewalk, and swing as you pass so the weapon connects. It is a dark-humour trophy in the classic GTA mould: a slow drive-by in a quiet street gives you the best chance of landing the hit without crashing. A motorcycle or a slow car works best, since you need to time the swing as you pass.
trophies.name: Ten Pin

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills are dirty cash you pick up from robberies and heists; they cannot be spent directly, so you take them to a contact who launders them into clean money for a cut. The $250,000 target is cumulative — keep laundering every batch of Marked Bills you earn and the total climbs. Bank vault robberies and armored trucks are good sources of Marked Bills, so this trophy pairs naturally with the robbery trophies.
trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops in Leonida. The total is cumulative and counts every shop in the game — clothing stores, gun shops, car mod shops, food and drink, and more. It adds up naturally over a full playthrough if you buy weapons, ammo, clothes, and vehicle upgrades, but you can also push it along by buying expensive items at Ammu-Nation or a high-end clothing store. The counter tracks lifetime spending, so there is no way to lose progress.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self

trophies.guide: Purchase all garage properties in Leonida. The starter data lists 8 garages; each one is a property you can buy from the in-game property or real-estate site, and each gives you vehicle storage. You will need a healthy bank balance, so save this for after the story when you have money from heists and laundered Marked Bills. Buy them one by one and the trophy pops when the last garage is purchased — check the property listings to find any you have not bought yet.
trophies.name: Little Boxes

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Scooter Bros is the game's vehicle delivery and registration app on the in-game phone: open it, register a vehicle you own or have found, and repeat until 10 are registered. The count is cumulative, so register every interesting vehicle you come across rather than saving it for later. The trophy pops as soon as the tenth vehicle is registered.
trophies.name: On the Spot
